paper.title: What Investment Data Implies about the AI Transition
paper.paper_claim: The five largest U.S. technology firms spent about USD 380bn on capital expenditures in 2025 and were forecast to spend about USD 755bn in 2026; the model maps the investment path through 2027 to an AI-sector productivity boom of roughly 2.7x.

hypothesis: The paper's central revealed-preference input, an approximately USD 755bn 2026 capex scale for Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle, remains supported by information available after the paper was issued.
acceptance_rule: CONDITION if a conservative post-paper cross-check remains at or above USD 755bn but definitions or fiscal periods prevent an exact apples-to-apples reconstruction; REJECT if the current comparable aggregate falls materially below USD 755bn; USE only after the paper model is rerun with harmonized capex definitions and periods.

conservative_cross_check.method: Use Amazon's officially confirmed approximately USD 200bn 2026 plan rather than the later USD 220bn management-call figure; use the low ends of Alphabet and Meta's latest guidance ranges; use Microsoft's approximately USD 175bn calendar-2026 expectation; use Oracle's latest completed FY2026 GAAP capital expenditures.

notes.Amazon: The latest Q2 management-call transcript reports about USD 220bn 2026 capital spending. Amazon's own February release and shareholder letter had already confirmed approximately USD 200bn; the conservative cross-check therefore uses USD 200bn.
notes.Alphabet: Q2 management updated FY2026 capex guidance to USD 195-205bn; midpoint USD 200bn is used here and USD 195bn in the conservative cross-check.
notes.Microsoft: FY2026 Q4 earnings call states calendar-year 2026 capex expectation of approximately USD 175bn after lease classification changes.
notes.Meta: Q2 2026 official release gives full-year 2026 capex guidance of USD 130-145bn including principal payments on finance leases; midpoint USD 137.5bn is used here and USD 130bn in the conservative cross-check.
notes.Oracle: Latest completed FY2026 GAAP capital expenditures were USD 55.663bn. Oracle has not provided a directly comparable calendar-2026 capex guide in the cited release, so this is not an exact period match.

source_quality: Primary company, SEC and NBER sources are used where they expose the needed values. Amazon's later USD 220bn and Alphabet's updated USD 195-205bn ranges are management-call transcript mirrors; the conservative test avoids depending on Amazon's later USD 220bn figure. Oracle remains a fiscal-period mismatch.
verdict_reason: Even the conservative cross-check totals USD 755.663bn, essentially matching and slightly exceeding the paper's USD 755bn premise. A midpoint/latest cross-check is about USD 788.2bn, roughly 4.4% higher. The observed investment scale therefore has not weakened. However, firm definitions differ, Oracle is on a fiscal-year actual rather than a calendar-year guide, and the 2.7x productivity result is produced by a nonlinear structural model. The capex premise is supported but the exact 2.7x productivity hurdle is not independently re-estimated here.
decision_use: Treat hyperscaler AI capex intensity as an unresolved valuation and capital-efficiency risk that remains at least as large as in the paper. Do not infer that higher capex itself proves future returns or productivity.
do_not_use_for: Recomputing the paper's 2.7x productivity factor by proportional scaling
Treating all capex as AI-only capex
Assuming identical accounting definitions across firms
next_test: Reconstruct a harmonized point-in-time 2025-2027 capex panel for the five firms from SEC filings and official guidance, then rerun the paper's break-even productivity calibration and compare it with realized cloud/AI revenue, operating income and free-cash-flow conversion.
